        one command: the site's records, its address, a running server, the page in a browser
  bonfyre site set NAME [--title T] [--tagline T] [--accent #hex] [--footnote T [--footnote-label L --footnote-link URL] | --no-footnote] | --presentation FILE.json   change a running site; the next page load shows it
  bonfyre site list [--json]
  bonfyre site show NAME|HOST [--json]
  bonfyre site search TEXT [--top N] [--json]      by meaning and by words, across every site
  bonfyre site page NAME --title T --text "..."|--file F   a standing page: served, in the menu, readable by assistants
                    [--group G]                      Markdown keeps its sections, code and tables; six pages or a group make a manual
  bonfyre site offer NAME --title T --price "$450 per project" --text "..." [--bookable]
        something the site sells: on its offers page, and readable by assistants; nothing takes payment
  bonfyre site accept NAME --request REF [--when T]  a request becomes a promise (commitments), an invoice (Pay), an opportunity (Finance)
  bonfyre site paid NAME --request REF --reference BANK-REF | done NAME --request REF | promises NAME
  bonfyre site domain NAME --to example.com [--ip A.B.C.D --secrets FILE [--apply]]
  bonfyre site post NAME --title T --text "..."      a dated post;  --withdraw ID takes one down
  bonfyre site page NAME --route /path --remove | --replace ...
  bonfyre site key NAME [--label WHO] [--write]      a key for one assistant, tried before it is handed over
  bonfyre site key NAME --withdraw WHO | keys NAME   withdraw a holder's key; who holds what
  bonfyre site share NAME [--stop]                   a public address for the site, tried from outside first
  bonfyre site usage NAME | inbox NAME               what assistants asked; messages left for the owner
  bonfyre site mcp NAME [--json]                   the site as an assistant's tool: stood up, checked, ready to paste
  bonfyre site check NAME [--json]                 dead links, unreadable colours, missing name or language
  bonfyre site export NAME --out FILE [--format html|wordpress|frappe]
        html: one self-contained page, fit to attach.  wordpress: its export file.  frappe: its documents
  bonfyre site import SOURCE --as NAME [--limit N]
        a WordPress address or export file, Frappe documents, any page address, or a file

  --home DIR      where this network of sites lives (default ~/.bonfyre/sites)
